title: Comparison of scheme and Galois pullbacks
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, let $X_0$ be a
finite-type $k_0$-scheme,
put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring
annihilated by an integer invertible in $k$. The $q$-power scheme
Frobenius $\Phi$ and the
geometric-Frobenius automorphism
$g_\gamma$ of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius] induce, on the
small pro-etale site of $X$,
natural isomorphisms of derived categories

$$
\kappa:L\Phi^*\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Lg_\gamma^*,
$$

and, for every $m\geq1$, a multiplicative iterate

$$
\kappa^{(m)}:L\Phi^m{}^*\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Lg_\gamma^{m*}.
$$

The isomorphisms are compatible with the factorization of
[prop-trf-frobenius-factorization]: scheme Frobenius and geometric
Galois Frobenius differ by a universal homeomorphism, namely the
absolute $q$-power Frobenius. (Source: the comparison between
geometric and arithmetic Frobenius, via the invariance of
the etale site under universal homeomorphisms, is the terminal interface
of the trace-formula chapter.)

note: *Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

proof.text:
Put $F=F_X$, $H_m=F^{am}$ and $g=g_\gamma$. The global datum gives $p$ prime, $a\geq1$ and $k_0=\mathbf F_q$. By [def-weil-finite-field-q-elements] this field has characteristic $p$. Its structure map to every section ring of the $k_0$-scheme $X$ sends $p\cdot1=0$ to $p\cdot1=0$, so $X$ is in characteristic $p$. By [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme], $H_m$ is absolute $q^m$-power Frobenius. The factorization [prop-trf-frobenius-factorization] says $H_m=g_\sigma^m\circ\Phi^m=\Phi^m\circ g_\sigma^m$. The current construction in [def-trf-scheme-frobenius] has $g=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma^{-1})$ and $g_\sigma=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$. Composing their affine ring maps gives the identity, so $g=g_\sigma^{-1}$. Composing on either side with $g^m$ gives
$$\Phi^m=g^m\circ H_m=H_m\circ g^m.$$
In particular $g$ commutes with $H_1$; no assertion that $g$ is a $k$-morphism is used.

source.place: first paragraph, factorization; second paragraph, factorization for every m

proof.text: The factor $H_m$ is a universal homeomorphism, including on nonreduced schemes. On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$ its ring map is $\varphi:R\to R$, $x\mapsto x^{p^{am}}$, by [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. If $\varphi(x)=0$, then $x$ is nilpotent. Every element $x$ of the target satisfies $x^{p^{am}}\in\varphi(R)$ and $p^{am}x=0\in\varphi(R)$. Apply [lem-pur-power-generated-spectrum-homeomorphism] with exponent $am>0$. Its base-change clause gives a homeomorphism after every affine base change. For an arbitrary $T\to X$, cover $T$ by affine opens mapping into affine opens of $X$; the preimages of these opens under the base change of $H_m$ are exactly those affine base changes. A map which is a homeomorphism over each open of a target cover is a homeomorphism: the local inverses agree on overlaps because each is the inverse of that map. This proves the universal condition of [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism].

source.place: Tag 0CC8, lemma-frobenius; affine input Tag 0BRA, algebra.tex, lemma-p-ring-map

proof.text: Work throughout with the constant finite ring $A$, not with an assumed presentation $A=A_{E,n}$. The coefficient-stage reference now included in the scheme-Frobenius definition does not assert that every finite $A$ has that presentation; the pullbacks for the arbitrary $A$ in this proposition are defined by the generic constant-coefficient operations cited in this step. For every scheme map $h$, [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] identifies $h^{-1}A$ with $A$, preserving constant sections. Thus [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] identifies the module pullback with exact inverse image with transported action. In the operations of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], $Lh^*$ is consequently this functor applied termwise to complexes. Exactness and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] show that this computes the functor on the entire unbounded category $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, with no constructibility or boundedness condition.

source.place: first paragraph, functoriality of derived pullback; exact constant-coefficient realization

proof.text: Use the canonical composition isomorphism $L(f\circ h)^*\simeq Lh^*Lf^*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Its coefficient hypothesis holds: the composite identification and the identification for $f\circ h$ both preserve constant sections by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. We verify the coherence needed below rather than assuming an unstated associativity clause. On sheaves the direct-image formula of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] identifies $(f\circ h)_*$ with $f_*h_*$ by the canonical isomorphism between the iterated fibre products. Combine the module adjunctions in that definition using [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], and take the unique inverse-image comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]. For three maps the two direct-image identifications have the same three fibre-product projections, hence are equal. The two composite Hom bijections are the same succession of three adjunction bijections, so the cited uniqueness makes their inverse-image comparisons equal. The identity-map comparison is the identity for the same reason. These ordinary comparisons are the canonical module pullback comparisons, since their adjuncts carry the single pullback unit to the two successive units. Apply them degreewise and use clauses (2) and (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to descend the isomorphisms and their coherence equations. The descended comparison is the cited derived comparison: on a K-flat complex both are the class of the canonical termwise module comparison, and [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] supplies a K-flat resolution with flat terms for every complex on this small ringed site, so agreement on those representatives gives agreement on all objects. Below products of pullbacks use these coherent comparisons.

source.place: first paragraph, pullback functoriality; explicit adjunction and localization argument

proof.text:
Let $P_m=L(H_m)^*$. By [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site] its canonical trivialization, iterated $am$ times, gives $t_m:P_m\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$. The last clause of [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback] specifies this same canonical trivialization for arbitrary finite constant $A$ and its composition law. Apply it with $b_1=am$ and $b_2=an$ to obtain, under Step 4's comparisons,
$$t_{m+n,K}=t_{n,K}\circ t_{m,P_nK}:P_mP_nK\longrightarrow K.$$
No boundedness, constructibility, or choice of a Frobenius structure on $K$ is used.

source.place: first paragraph, canonical trivialization iterated a times; second paragraph, composition of relative Frobenius maps (Stacks Tag 0F6W)

proof.text:
Write $G_m=L(g^m)^*$ and $T_m=L(\Phi^m)^*$. Combining Step 1 with Step 4 gives $T_m\simeq P_mG_m$. Define, for every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$,
$$\kappa^{(m)}_K:T_mK\xrightarrow{\sim}P_mG_mK\xrightarrow{t_{m,G_mK}}G_mK.$$
This is a natural isomorphism since both arrows are natural isomorphisms. For $m=1$ it is the required $\kappa$. This is precisely the comparison obtained by cancelling absolute Frobenius in $\Phi^m=g^mH_m$; Step 2 supplies the universal-homeomorphism clause.

source.place: first paragraph, displayed construction of kappa; second paragraph, same construction for m

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback] to $X=Y$, $u=g^n$ and $b=am$. The definition [def-trf-scheme-frobenius] makes $g^n$ a scheme automorphism; in particular it is a scheme morphism between characteristic-$p$ schemes. Its coefficient identification is precisely the constant one fixed in Step 3. With $G_n=L(g^n)^*$, the cited statement gives, for its canonical composition comparison $c_{g^n,am}:G_nP_m\xrightarrow{\sim}P_mG_n$,
$$t_{m,G_nK}\circ c_{g^n,am,K}=G_n(t_{m,K}).$$
This is the needed compatibility with the semilinear Galois map; it follows from the statement's pullback-naturality clause, not from the weaker open-restriction clause of the absolute-Frobenius-site node. Interchanging $m$ and $n$ gives the comparison $G_mP_n\cong P_nG_m$ used in Step 8.

source.place: second paragraph, composition of relative Frobenius maps; pullback naturality supplied by the existing general 0F6W interface

proof.text:
Let $m,n\geq1$. Since $H_n=H_1^n$, the commutation in Step 1 gives $H_n\circ g^m=g^m\circ H_n$. Thus the equality of scheme morphisms underlying the comparisons below is
$$\Phi^{m+n}=(g^n\circ H_n)\circ(g^m\circ H_m)=g^{m+n}\circ H_{m+n}.$$
The middle interchange is exactly the equality defining the commutation comparison of Step 7 with its indices interchanged. Consequently Step 4's coherence identifies the composite comparison with the one used to define $\kappa^{(m+n)}$ in Step 6. In particular,
$$T_{m+n}=T_mT_n\simeq P_mG_mP_nG_n\simeq P_mP_nG_mG_n.$$
Before commuting $G_mP_n$, the composite $G_m(\kappa^{(n)}_K)\circ\kappa^{(m)}_{T_nK}$ is $G_m(t_{n,G_nK})\circ t_{m,G_mP_nG_nK}$. Let $d:G_mP_n\xrightarrow{\sim}P_nG_m$ be Step 7 with its indices interchanged. That step gives $G_m(t_{n,G_nK})=t_{n,G_mG_nK}\circ d_{G_nK}$, while naturality gives $d_{G_nK}\circ t_{m,G_mP_nG_nK}=t_{m,P_nG_mG_nK}\circ P_m(d_{G_nK})$. Thus the composite, after the displayed identification of its domain by $P_m(d)$, becomes
$$P_mP_nG_mG_nK\xrightarrow{t_{m,P_nG_mG_nK}}P_nG_mG_nK\xrightarrow{t_{n,G_mG_nK}}G_mG_nK.$$
The iterate identity of [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback] identifies this with $t_{m+n,G_{m+n}K}$. Hence
$$\kappa^{(m+n)}_K=G_m(\kappa^{(n)}_K)\circ\kappa^{(m)}_{T_nK}.$$
This is the multiplicative-iterate law, with $\kappa^{(1)}=\kappa$; induction on $m$ shows that the comparison for $\Phi^m$ is the multiplicative iterate of $\kappa$. All equations were obtained on module sheaves or degreewise on complexes; [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] transfers them to the unbounded derived categories. By Step 6 this multiplicative family is the one from the stated Frobenius factorizations, completing all clauses.

source.place: second paragraph, multiplicative iterate and addition of exponents

proof_origin.place: Both paragraphs, with explicit composition coherence and multiplicative-iterate calculation

$$

$$

and, for every $m\geq1$, a multiplicative iterate

$$

proof.text:
Write $F_X^{(q)}$ for absolute $q$-power Frobenius.
The canonical trivialization of
[lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site], iterated $a$ times, gives
$L(F_X^{(q)})^*\simeq\operatorname{id}$.
The factorization [prop-trf-frobenius-factorization] gives
$\Phi=g_\gamma F_X^{(q)}$, where $g_\gamma=g_\sigma^{-1}$
as in [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Thus functoriality of pullback
and this specified trivialization give

$$
L\Phi^*=L(F_X^{(q)})^*Lg_\gamma^*
\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg_\gamma^*.
$$

This defines $\kappa$. For $\Phi^m=g_\gamma^mF_X^{(q^m)}$ the
same construction is the multiplicative iterate $\kappa^{(m)}$:
the relative Frobenius maps compose to the corresponding power maps.
The resulting identifications therefore respect both the
factorization and addition of the exponents.
